thread:
alex: :rotating_light: noticing p99 jump in us-east-1 for streaming endpoints. Alerting here.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT 2026-04-12T14:05Z - latency.p99.us-east-1 crossed 3s (ID: INC-1907654321) — paging @oncall-engineer.

jasper: picking up the page. seeing a p95 ~ 600ms -> 900ms, p99 spiking to ~3.2s on the streaming route. Any recent deploys?

maria: no deploys in the last hour. autoscaler looks fine. console shows some nodes with abnormally high GPU temp.

eva: I can pull node logs. quick check: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` — some streaming workers on gpu-node-3 are in CrashLoopBackOff.

samir: checking GPU telemetry: `nvml` shows ECC_CORRECTABLE increasing and thermal_throttle flags true on gpu-node-3. forwarding telemetry snapshot.

alex: copying telemetry snippet: ```[gpu-node-3] ecc_correctable=12 ecc_uncorrectable=1 temp_C=95 thermal_throttle=1 clock_slowdown=2```

jasper: that looks like noisy ECC + thermal throttling. Could be a flaky GPU or airflow issue. Need to remove node from rotation and failover traffic.

maria: agree. plan: 1) taint/drain gpu-node-3 2) scale up standby pool 3) reroute traffic 4) open ticket with hw vendor.

infra-bot: Suggested drain command: ```kubectl drain gpu-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```

jasper: executing drain now. will cordon first: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-3` -> done. starting drain...

support-bot: Customer impact: 12 live streams reported increased latency, 2 retries surfaced in support queue (cust-1012, cust-1819). ETA to mitigate expected 10-15m after drain completes.

eva: drain progress: eviction of 24 pods, 18 succeeded, 6 pending due to local data. forcing eviction on streaming workers.

alex: while drain is happening, can we add a routing rule to prefer us-west endpoints for new sessions? Would reduce p99 immediately.

maria: yes, updating routing policy: `traffic-router set-preference region=us-west for=streaming-service weight=0.9` -> pushed. Should see fewer new sessions in us-east.

samir: GPU telemetry after drain start: ECC errors still accumulating before pods fully rescheduled. suspect a single GPU card is exhibiting intermittent ECC spikes.

jasper: drain finished. node is drained and cordoned. verifying load: p99 dropped from 3.2s -> 1.1s for streaming route. p95 back to ~350ms.

alex: great. mark node as quarantined for hardware investigation. `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-3 hardware/faulty=true:NoSchedule`

infra-bot: Node tainted. Also created infra ticket INF-6392 to schedule hardware swap and run vendor diagnostics.

maria: open hardware ticket and include nvml logs + dmesg output. tagging @samir to collect logs.

samir: logs collected and uploaded to INF-6392. notable: repeated `GPU ECC corrected` entries and `PCIe AER` warnings in dmesg within spillover window.

eva: running quick health sweep on other nodes; no similar patterns currently. possible single-card degradation.

support-bot: update for customers: "We experienced transient latency on streaming in us-east-1 from 14:05–14:22 UTC due to degraded GPU hardware. We routed new sessions to other regions and completed mitigation. We're investigating and will follow up with a timeline for hardware replacement." Draft ready for approval.

jasper: approve the customer note, send now.

support-bot: Message sent to affected customers and internal SLAs updated. Noted 99th percentile breach recorded for the window.

alex: on-call handoff in 20m. jasper, can you start the writeup and own postmortem?

jasper: yes, will start a short incident report and assign postmortem. initial notes: root cause = GPU card exhibiting ECC + thermal throttle leading to degraded processing and increased tail latency. Impact = elevated p99 on streaming; small set of customers saw retries and higher latency; mitigation = drained/cordoned node, shifted traffic, tainted node for hardware triage.

maria: add follow-ups: - schedule preventive firmware update across fleet - check data center cooling for gpu-node-3 rack - add automated alert for ECC rate > 5/min to page SRE earlier - add circuit breaker for streaming tail latency to offload to CPU fallback for short-lived sessions.

samir: contacting vendor now for RMA. INF-6392 is updated with serial + logs. Vendor responded with next-step remote diagnostics window tomorrow.

alex: handoff: jasper -> maria at 14:25 UTC. jasper will continue postmortem doc; maria will be primary on-call for any further action.

jasper: leaving notes in #postmortems and tagging the engineering PM. I'll attach commands we ran and telemetry charts.

maria: thanks team. closing incident channel once postmortem draft is up. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Incident INC-1907654321 marked RESOLVED at 14:22 UTC. Postmortem owner: jasper."
